title: CLO Tips Classroom - CLO X UE Integration Process
description: From downloading the UE plugin to exporting the final render, CLO technical experts teach you how to easily master the CLO and UE integration workflow!
transcript:
This video will explain how to use the LiveSync plugin to easily establish the connection between CLO and Unreal Engine (UE).

First, download UE.  
Search for Epic.  
Go to the official Epic website.  
Click to log in.  
If you don't have an Epic account, you need to register using an email.  
If you already have an account, just click to log in.  
After logging in, click the upper left corner.  
Find the virtual machine, then click to get the virtual machine.  
We can directly click to download the program.  
If you have any questions about the installation method,  
you can also click to view the installation guide.  
This is the official recorded tutorial on how to install UE.  
Now we can click to download the installation program.  

Below are the UE installation configuration requirements.  
Here are the graphics card and processor requirements for Windows systems.  
This is the requirement for Mac computers.  
You can check whether your computer’s configuration meets the UE installation requirements.  

After downloading the program,  
go to the download folder.  
Find the Epic Games program.  
Double-click to open it.  
A pop-up window like this will appear.  
You can install the program on a drive other than C.  
This way, we can save space on the C drive.  
Choose a folder and click confirm.  
At this time,  
the Epic Games program will appear on your desktop.  

After the installation is complete,  
the program window will open.  
Log in to your Epic account.  
This account is the same as the Epic Games account registered on the Epic official website.  
The accounts are the same.  

After logging in,  
you will see an interface like this.  
Here is the account information.  
Then enter the Unreal Engine.  
Find the engine version to add here.  
Click to add.  
Or just click to install the engine.  
Click to add.  
Click to install.  

Since the installation method of LiveSync after UE 5.6 is different,  
two installation methods will be explained.  

Let’s look at the first case,  
using UE 5.6.1 as an example.  
Here,  
you need to set the installation location of the engine.  
I also choose to install it on a drive other than C,  
to save C drive space.  
Note that there should be no Chinese or special characters in the engine installation path.  
You can use English or Pinyin characters.  
Click to install.  
Installation takes some time.  

We can install multiple versions of UE.  
If you continue to click to add,  
you can install different versions of UE.  

This is the installation progress.  
If we want to pause,  
click this button.  
You can also click to cancel the installation directly.  

Here you can see the download progress.  
This is the download progress.  
Here is the location of all the project files.  
FAB Library.  
This is the 3D assets added in FAB.  
These are some of the 3D assets I added before.  
If you are installing for the first time,  
these three fields are blank.  

Next, download CLO’s LiveSync plugin.  
Enter Connect Business.  
Then find the application.  
Find LiveSync.  
Then click to download.  
Select LiveSync to download the corresponding version.  

Starting from LiveSync 2.0.1,  
it will jump to FAB Business.  
You can directly add it to My Library here.  
After entering My Library,  
you can click to check in the launcher.  
Open and refresh.  
You can see CLO MD’s LiveSync plugin.  
Click to install the engine.  
You will see a prompt now.  
The plugin slot is for 5.6.  
Click to install.  
Installation takes some time.  
It is now installed in the 5.6 engine.  

Next, we will install another plugin.  
Enter FAB and click to search for Substance.  
Then find this plugin.  
It is next to My Library here.  
Click to search.  
Next, it appears in My Library.  
Following the goal with an asterisk,  
it will install.  
Yes, it’s finally installed.  
The plugin is fully installed.  

Next, with the remaining steps,  
by clicking to show it to CLO,  
then select 5.6.  
You can see the engine versions it supports.  
Then click Install.  

I just demonstrated how to install LiveSync in UE 5.6.  
Now I will introduce you to  
how to install LiveSync before UE 5.6.  

First, add another engine version.  
We can add 5.5.  
Then click Install.  
Also modify the installation path.  
Click Install.  

After installation is complete,  
follow the same method.  
First, install Substance.  
If the first installation is 5.5,  
follow the same steps.  
Search Substance 3D for Unreal Engine in FAB.  
Add it to the library.  
It will appear in our FAB Library.  

Next, follow the same method.  
Click Install to Engine.  
Now it uses 5.5 to add the plugin.  
Then click Install.  

Now our Substance plugin  
has been installed in UE 5.5.  

Next,  
let’s download LiveSync plugin for 5.5.  
Open the LiveSync interface.  
You can see the plugin version corresponding to 5.5.  
The LiveSync version downloaded is 2.0.0.  
It also corresponds to  
our CLO version 20.25.0.1.28.  
Click it directly.  
It will download a compressed package for us.  

After the compressed package is downloaded,  
double-click to open it.  
Extract the files.  

After extraction is complete,  
go back to this interface,  
then enter this guide.  
This is how to set up Unreal Engine  
and LiveSync plugin instructions.  

After extraction is complete,  
we need to add this file  
to this UE directory.  

What you need to pay attention to is:  
if we installed UE on a drive other than C,  
for example,  
I installed it on the A drive,  
we need to find this path on the A drive.  

Now let’s find the path.  
This is the path where I installed UE 5.5.  
Double-click to enter.  
Find the Engine folder.  
Then find Plugins.  
Then find the marked location.  

What you need to pay attention to here is:  
this folder is created after installing a certain plugin.  
It will be here to create a folder.  
Then you can see  
there is a Substance folder.  
This is the Substance plugin we just installed.  

If we haven’t installed a plugin in advance,  
this folder will not be created.  

Now we need to install the plugin.  
Find this folder  
that we just extracted.  
Copy it.  
Paste it here.  
Now we have pasted this plugin.  

Next,  
we need to set up these plugins in UE.  
Open the drive.  
Then click Start.  
This is the UE window of a new project.  

Next, create a project.  
First, set the project location.  
I set it on the A drive.  
The project name needs to be in English.  
Do not use special characters.  
Simply type the project name.  
Then click Create.  

Now the initial project opens.  
Click Edit.  
Click Paste.  
This is the plugin window.  
Search CLO.  
This is CLO’s plugin. It needs to be restarted now.  
We will not restart it for the time being, as we still need to search for another Substance plugin.  
We also need to hook it up.  
After hooking up is complete, close the window.  

Let’s set up some other options.  
We still need to find the Editor and then Project Settings.  
Let’s search for “Rui.”  
Then drag it to the bottom.  
Select X11 here.  
Then search for Translucent.  
In this option, part of the object is semi-transparent.  
Then hook it up.  

After setting these options,  
click Restart Immediately.  
Restarting takes some time.  

After restarting, check the plugins.  
Find the Editor again.  
Click on Plugins to check installation.  
We can see that our CLO plugin and Substance plugin have been installed.  

Now open CLO.  
Then open a project file.  
This project file must ensure  
the simulation function in CLO is turned off.  
And CLO needs to be in simulation mode or UV editing mode.  
Ensure CLO does not have any animation currently being recorded.  

It is recommended to change the object name to the text name.  
This will speed up the import.  

I have already recorded an animation in advance.  
Now let’s play and check.  
This is an animation that walks around the place.  
If we press this button, the animation will stop and show the selected file.  

Now point it.  
Now we need to switch to casual mode,  
which is the normal time mode.  
Enable the basic default mode,  
which is active mode.  

Let’s refresh the Welcome window.  
Just wait for the video to load.  
You can hear the music playing  
when you open the key “i” button.  

Save is the save button.  
Click this button.  
The saved resources will be saved according to the saved settings of clothing, model, scene, and props, and stored in the specified folder in the Content Browser.  

This button, S-Close, can save KS-Close resources.  
LiveSync Connection Status can be saved according to the connection status with CLO.  
LiveSync Connection Status will display green or red dots.  
Now it shows a green dot,  
which means it can successfully import the files opened in CLO.  

If it shows red dots, we need to check whether the versions are correct:  
the LiveSync version you downloaded,  
the UE version,  
and the CLO version—  
are they compatible?  

If it still shows red after checking,  
you can try some simple operations in CLO,  
for example, click on the paper,  
or adjust the clothing.  

If it still doesn’t work,  
you can restart CLO,  
and then check the options below.  

This is the grid.  
This is the texture.  

Next, let’s look at the garment options.  
This option includes clothing.  
If you select this option,  
you can import clothing from CLO into UE.  

These two options below:  
one is Single Object,  
the other is Multiple Objects.  

If you choose Single Object,  
the clothing is a complete mesh,  
an integrated mesh.  

If you choose Multiple Objects,  
each panel or component is independent.  

Now,  
I choose Single Object.  

These two options below represent Thin and Thick.  
They correspond to the display mode of the CLO texture surface.  
The Thin option represents the texture surface,  
and the Thick option represents a thicker texture surface display.  

The option below is Unified UV Coordinates.  
If you select this option,  
the UV coordinates will be unified.  

If we use this option,  
we need to preview the clothing in CLO,  
including garment simulation data.  

This means it contains clothing simulation data,  
which is the same as the option in CLO.  

Using this option,  
we save the clothing as the highest number of Kiosk Cloth resources.  

This function can manually read the material in the UV.  

This option, Include Cache Animation,  
includes animation data from CLO.  
If there is animation in CLO,  
you can choose this option.  
It can bring animation clothing data into the UV,  
and save it as a combined animation.  

If the clothing and models  
need to be imported, click on this icon.  
Our costume and model can be played in UE.  

Next, look at the options after Avatar.  
What about this?  
This option includes Avatar and virtual models.  
If we check this option, we can import virtual models from CLO into UE.  
Since CLO models have bone joints, they will be saved as a bone network.  

This option is Avatar Animation.  
After selecting this option, the model’s animation will also be imported.  
Selecting this will display joint animation and save the animation.  

Then, at the bottom, are Scene and Props.  
If we select this,  
when CLO contains this animation,  
it will display 3D resources of the scene and props.  
We can import scenes and props into UE.  

Override Transparent Blend Mode is Transparent Blend Mode.  
The two options at the bottom are semi-transparent and opaque.  
This can be created by LiveSync.  
For costume materials, choose a material blend mode.  

Next, select the desired option according to our needs.  
For this option,  
I will choose a single mesh.  
Then, choose the second option.  
Since our project file contains animation,  
I will choose Animation.  
Our model also contains animation,  
so I choose Model Animation.  
Then choose Joint Animation.  

After choosing,  
click Update.  
You will see a window like this,  
which is what I just explained.  

Some things to pay attention to:  
First, ensure the simulation function in CLO is enabled.  
Ensure CLO is in simulation mode or UV editor mode.  
Ensure CLO does not have any animation currently being recorded.  
Then click OK.  

Now, our model and costume  
are imported into the UE window.  
Click the window that appears.  
You can check it.  
Our model and costume  
are visible on the large screen.  

You can see the imported project file.  
It is a USB format file.  
It will be divided into model files.  
Naomi is our model file.  

Then there are the costume files.  
They will be divided into these two files.  
Click the triangle to collapse them.  

Next, click Save.  
Save our model and costume files.  

Before saving,  
you can first create a new folder named CLO.  
Click New Folder.  
Then click Save.  
Find the created folder.  
Click OK.  

You need to wait a moment.  
After saving,  
the UE window will become blank.  

Next, let’s see  
how to import and use the saved costume and model files in UE.  

Go back to selection mode.  
In the Content Browser,  
find the just saved folder.  
This is our costume file.  
The file name is the same as the project file.  
It contains the garment costume file,  
which is an integrated storage with materials.  

There is also an animation sequence for the model  
and the model’s physical assets.  
These are parts of the costume.  
Google’s web font and other files are included.  
There are also patterns.  
This is a pattern of the model.  

Next, I will explain how to store the completed costume and model files  
to be used in UE.  

Open the first file clip.  
Drag it to the UE window.  
Then open the third folder.  
Drag the first animation sequence in.  
In the position here, click to reset values to default.  
Then click to reset the values to default again.  

Now the costume is worn on the model.  
Click the activated frame editor to play this frame in the viewport.  
Move the view, you can see  
we recorded a good animation  
playing in the UE window.  

Press Esc to exit.  
Open again.  
This is a scene file built in advance.  
Open the Content Browser.  
Place the model and costume in the scene file.  

Select the costume file, then scale.  
In Position and Rotation, click the back button to reset values to default.  
Select the model file and do the same.  

At the same time, select the model and costume files.  
Drag the move tool to move the files to the desired position.  
Adjust the scale to the correct size.  
Use the rotation tool to rotate the files to the correct position.  

Click to run the structure to see the effect.  
Select the camera.  
In the viewport, select Stage Animation Playback.  
Click to play the animation.  
Very good.  

Press F11 to maximize the current viewport.  
Switch to quiet mode.  
You can move the mouse to view the entire scene.  

Finally, choose an ideal view.  
Click the upper left corner button.  
Choose High Resolution Screenshot.  
Enter the desired screenshot size.  
Click Capture.  
Quickly output the current effect image.  

Finally, you can view the performance of CLO’s clothing in the UE scene.  

Thanks for watching and see you in the next video.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Classroom - CLO X UE Integration Process
chunks.content: ## Overview of CLO and Unreal Engine (UE) Integration with LiveSync This section explains the process of connecting CLO with Unreal Engine (UE) using the LiveSync plugin. It covers the necessary software downloads, installation steps, and compatibility considerations for establishing a seamless integration between CLO and UE. --- ## Downloading and Installing Unreal Engine (UE) This section details how to download and install Unreal Engine (UE), including system requirements and configuration tips. - Visit the official Epic Games website and log in using your Epic account. If you do not have an account, register with an email. - After logging in, download the Epic Games Launcher. - You may install the program on any drive other than C: to save space. - The Epic Games Launcher shortcut will appear on your desktop after installation. - Log in using the same Epic account credentials. - In the launcher, navigate to the Unreal Engine tab. - Add and install the desired engine version(s). - UE supports installing multiple versions simultaneously. - Installation progress can be paused or canceled. - Ensure your system meets the minimum requirements for UE installation: - Windows: Specific GPU and processor requirements (refer to Epic's official documentation). - Mac: Compatible hardware specifications. --- ## Installing LiveSync and Substance Plugins for UE 5.6 and Later This section explains how to install the LiveSync plugin and the Substance plugin in Unreal Engine version 5.6.1 and later. - Locate LiveSync within Connect Business and download the appropriate version. - Starting from LiveSync 2.0.1, integration shifts to FAB Business where you add the plugin to "My Library" and install it via the launcher. - Select the plugin slot corresponding to your UE version (e.g., 5.6). - The Substance 3D plugin for UE can be found and installed similarly through FAB. - After installation, verify that both plugins appear in your UE plugin list. - You can install plugins for multiple UE versions by repeating the process for each version. --- ## Installing LiveSync and Plugins for UE Versions Before 5.6 This section covers the manual installation process for UE versions before 5.6, such as 5.5. - Download LiveSync version 2.0.0 for UE 5.5, corresponding to CLO version 20.25.0.1.28. - Extract the compressed LiveSync package. - Locate the Unreal Engine installation directory (e.g., A:\Drive\UE_5.5). - Navigate to `Engine > Plugins`. - If the Plugins folder is empty, it indicates no plugins are installed yet. - Paste the extracted LiveSync plugin folder into the Plugins directory. - Open UE and create a new project: - Set project location (avoid C: if space is limited). - Use English characters for project names; no special characters. - In UE, open the Plugins window, search for CLO and Substance plugins. - Enable the plugins but delay restarting UE until both are enabled. - Adjust project settings by searching for specific options: - Drag ‘X11’ to the bottom (specific setting context). - Locate and configure ‘Translucent’ settings for semi-transparent object rendering. - Restart UE to apply plugin changes.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Classroom - CLO X UE Integration Process
chunks.content: - Open UE and create a new project: - Set project location (avoid C: if space is limited). - Use English characters for project names; no special characters. - In UE, open the Plugins window, search for CLO and Substance plugins. - Enable the plugins but delay restarting UE until both are enabled. - Adjust project settings by searching for specific options: - Drag ‘X11’ to the bottom (specific setting context). - Locate and configure ‘Translucent’ settings for semi-transparent object rendering. - Restart UE to apply plugin changes. - Confirm both CLO and Substance plugins are active in the Plugins window. --- ## Preparing CLO for LiveSync Integration This section explains the necessary CLO settings before importing data into UE. - Open CLO and load the desired project file. - Disable the simulation function in CLO. - CLO must be in simulation mode or UV editing mode. - Ensure no animation is currently recording in CLO. - Rename objects with text-based names for faster import. - Verify existing animations; use the play button to test and stop animations as needed. - Refresh the LiveSync Welcome window to establish connection status. --- ## LiveSync Connection Status and Troubleshooting This section describes how to monitor and troubleshoot LiveSync connection between CLO and UE. - The LiveSync Connection Status indicator shows green (connected) or red (disconnected). - If red: - Check compatibility of LiveSync version, UE version, and CLO version. - Perform simple CLO operations (e.g., clicking objects, adjusting clothing). - Restart CLO if issues persist. - Additional options: - Grid and texture display toggles. - Garment import options (Single Object vs. Multiple Objects). - Texture display modes (Thin for surface texture, Thick for thicker display). - Unified UV Coordinates option to unify UV mapping and include garment simulation data. - Include Cache Animation option to import animation data from CLO. - Avatar options: - Import virtual models (avatars) with bone networks. - Avatar Animation option imports model joint animations. - Scene and Props option imports 3D scene elements and props. - Override Transparent Blend Mode configures material transparency (semi-transparent or opaque). --- ## Importing and Updating CLO Models and Costumes in UE This section explains how to import CLO models, costumes, and animations into UE and update them using LiveSync. - Choose import options based on project needs (e.g., Single Mesh, Animation, Model Animation, Joint Animation). - After selection, click Update. - Confirm CLO is in proper mode and no animations are recording. - Imported models and costumes appear in UE’s viewport. - Project files are saved in USB format, separated into model and costume files. - Organize files by creating a CLO folder within UE’s Content Browser before saving. - After saving, UE viewport may blank temporarily. --- ## Using Saved CLO Assets in Unreal Engine This section explains how to utilize saved CLO garment and model files within UE projects. - Navigate to the saved CLO folder in UE’s Content Browser.
chunks.content_description: From downloading the UE plugin to exporting the final render, CLO technical experts teach you how to easily master the CLO and UE integration workflow!

chunks.title: CLO Tips Classroom - CLO X UE Integration Process
chunks.content: - Imported models and costumes appear in UE’s viewport. - Project files are saved in USB format, separated into model and costume files. - Organize files by creating a CLO folder within UE’s Content Browser before saving. - After saving, UE viewport may blank temporarily. --- ## Using Saved CLO Assets in Unreal Engine This section explains how to utilize saved CLO garment and model files within UE projects. - Navigate to the saved CLO folder in UE’s Content Browser. - Locate garment costume files (with integrated materials) and animation sequences. - Drag model files and animation sequences into the UE viewport. - Reset position and rotation values to default. - Apply costumes to models by dragging animations to models. - Use frame editor to play and preview animations. - Position, scale, and rotate models and costumes using UE’s transform tools. - Place models and costumes within scene files. - Adjust scale and position as needed. - Use UE’s Stage Animation Playback and camera controls to view animations in the scene. - Maximize viewport with F11 and enter quiet mode for easier navigation. - Capture high-resolution screenshots using the upper left corner menu: - Specify resolution. - Click Capture to export images. --- ## Summary of Best Practices and Recommendations - Always install Unreal Engine on a drive with sufficient space, preferably not the system C drive. - Avoid Chinese characters or special characters in installation paths and project names; use English or Pinyin. - Verify plugin versions are compatible with your CLO and UE versions. - Use LiveSync version 2.0.1 or later for UE 5.6 and above; use manual extraction for earlier UE versions. - Rename CLO objects with clear text names to optimize import speed. - Disable CLO simulation and animation recording before importing. - Use appropriate import options in LiveSync to control mesh type, UV handling, and animation inclusion. - Regularly check LiveSync connection status and troubleshoot by restarting CLO or adjusting settings. - Organize UE assets by creating dedicated folders for CLO projects. - Utilize UE’s animation playback and viewport tools to preview and refine imported assets. --- This document provides a comprehensive guide for setting up, installing, and using the CLO LiveSync plugin with Unreal Engine to enable real-time garment and model integration, animation handling, and scene setup.
